question.:question/problem: If $f(x) = \frac{\cos x}{\ln x}$, find $f^{\prime}(x)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\cos{\left(x \right)}$ and $v(x)=\ln{\left(x \right)}.$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x)&=\frac{u^{\prime}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot v^{\prime}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(\cos{\left(x \right)})^{\prime}\cdot (\ln{\left(x \right)})-(\cos{\left(x \right)})\cdot (\ln{\left(x \right)})^{\prime}}{(\ln{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(- \sin{\left(x \right)})\cdot (\ln{\left(x \right)})-(\cos{\left(x \right)})\cdot (\frac{1}{x})}{(\ln{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{- \ln{\left(x \right)} \sin{\left(x \right)} - \frac{\cos{\left(x \right)}}{x}}{\ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}}\\ &=- \frac{x \ln{\left(x \right)} \sin{\left(x \right)} + \cos{\left(x \right)}}{x \ln{\left(x \right)}^{2}}\end{aligned}
